name: Com poi
summary: Cơm pồi is named by Phong Nha-Ke Bang National Park for Chứt communities and for Nguồn people who live mainly in Minh Hóa. The Quang Binh visitor portal’s accounts do not agree on the grain, the pot, or the spelling cơm bồi.
origin: Chứt and Nguồn cooking in the Phong Nha-Ke Bang buffer, including Minh Hóa. The park names the dish. The visitor portal’s articles disagree on the method.
culture: The park’s culture note ties cơm pồi to Chứt community life, custom, and festivals, and also lists it among Nguồn dishes with ốc vặn and ốc núi.
texture: The 15 April 2025 article says the steamed corn-and-cassava version is airy. The 28 October 2014 article says the charcoal bamboo tube has the scent of the bamboo skin, the chew of sticky rice, and the richness of the other grains. The 13 March 2024 article, which spells it cơm bồi, says the sliced cake is yellow and fragrant.
taste: The 13 March 2024 article describes a rich taste of corn and cassava with a light sweetness. The 15 April 2025 article also serves it with salt, crushed chili, and lime leaves.
howToEat: The 15 April 2025 article pounds corn and cassava, steams them, and says the shape follows the steamer. It is eaten with vegetable soup cooked with fish and snails, or with salt, crushed chili, and lime leaves. At a family meal it is rolled into small balls.

The 28 October 2014 article uses corn soaked about half a day, upland sticky-rice flour, and pressed cassava, packed with a little water and salt into a bamboo tube stopped with forest banana leaf. The tube sits on charcoal about an hour. The same article also describes boiling the tubes, or steaming the mix in a wooden chõ. Elder A Hui Tăng of Dân Hóa, then 79, said charcoal is the method people prefer. It was eaten with forest-vegetable soup cooked with fish, snails, or forest meat.

The 13 March 2024 article spells the dish cơm bồi. Dried corn is soaked in hot water for two to three hours, pounded, and sifted. Fresh cassava is shredded, pressed, mixed with the corn flour, steamed, and sliced. It is eaten with ốc đực and cà lào from streams and forest.
The 15 April 2025 article says visitors eat it at evening meals in homes in làng Tân Háa, Minh Hóa. A shop door, an hour, and a price are Check on arrival.
where: Chứt communities in the park buffer, and Nguồn people who live mainly in Minh Hóa. The 15 April 2025 article names làng Tân Háa. A stall address in Phong Nha village is Check on arrival.
seoTitle: Com poi — three accounts, one dish name
seoDescription: The park names cơm pồi for Chứt and Nguồn cooking. Portal articles disagree on sticky rice, bamboo, and the spelling cơm bồi. A price is Check on arrival.
